mainTopic: Does designation (הזמנה) for the dead make an item forbidden? אביי and רבא's sources, and a series of challenges and proofs testing their מחלוקת
overview: The גמרא is in the middle of a מחלוקת between אביי and רבא: does designating something for a dead person (הזמנה), like weaving shrouds, make it forbidden? אביי says yes and learns it from עגלה ערופה. רבא says no and learns it from עבודה זרה. The amud first explains why each one rejects the other's source. It then gives a סימן and brings a series of cases against רבא: a scarf set aside for a ספר תורה, a monument with a row added for the dead, and a grave dug for a father. Each time the גמרא defends רבא, either by showing a real action was done or by giving another reason, such as כבוד אביו. Along the way, רב חסדא teaches that a cloth for תפילין becomes restricted only with both designation and use. Next the גמרא tries to prove רבא's view from a new grave and from leftover burial money. Both proofs are pushed away, and the משנה about leftover money turns out to fit both אביי and רבא. The amud ends by opening a new proof attempt: parents throwing garments onto their son's bier.

steps.title: Why רבא learns from עבודה זרה and not from עגלה ערופה
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that accessories to the dead should be learned from accessories of עבודה זרה. עגלה ערופה is different because the calf itself is holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn the rules of accessories from the rules of accessories. That leaves out עגלה ערופה, where the calf itself is holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering why רבא does not learn from עגלה ערופה. Shrouds are accessories (משמשין) to the dead, so they should be compared to accessories of עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shrouds only serve the dead person. They are not the main subject. In עבודה זרה, the animal offered to the idol is also only an accessory, so the comparison fits. The עגלה ערופה is the main item of its own ceremony, so it is not a good model for accessories.

keyTerms.meaning: Accessories, items that serve something else
We learn (one law from another)
To exclude, to leave out
The calf whose neck is broken when a murder victim is found and the killer is unknown
Its very body is holy

phrases.english: We learn accessories from accessories,
phrases.notes: The shrouds serve the dead person, and the animal offered to an idol serves the idol.

phrases.english: which excludes the עגלה ערופה,
since it itself is holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to the question just before this section, which asked why רבא does not learn from עגלה ערופה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the sources: accessories versus the main holy item
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps רבא should also learn from עגלה ערופה, as אביי does.
steps.terutzMaskana: Shrouds are accessories, so they are learned from accessories of עבודה זרה. The עגלה ערופה is itself holy and does not compare.

steps.title: Why doesn't אביי learn from עבודה זרה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks the mirror question about אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי, why doesn't he learn from עבודה זרה?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that רבא's reasoning is clear, the גמרא asks why אביי does not use רבא's source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא just made a strong case that accessories should be learned from accessories. So the גמרא needs to explain why אביי still prefers עגלה ערופה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Idol worship

phrases.english: And אביי, what is the reason
that he does not learn from idol worship?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַבָּיֵי, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא גָּמַר מֵעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors the question that was just answered for רבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why אביי rejects עבודה זרה as the source for the law of shrouds

steps.title: אביי: learn a proper practice from a proper practice
steps.stepSummary: אביי prefers to learn burial, which is a proper מצוה, from עגלה ערופה, which is also a מצוה. He will not learn it from idol worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would say to you: we learn something that is a proper practice from something that is a proper practice. That leaves out idol worship, which is not a proper practice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for אביי. Burying the dead and the עגלה ערופה ceremony are both proper מצוות, so they belong together. Idol worship does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each אמורא has a different reason for picking his source. רבא looks at the type of object, meaning an accessory. אביי looks at the type of activity, meaning a proper מצוה. That difference explains why they learn from different places.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say to you
Something that is a proper, normal practice
Which is not a proper practice

steps.whatToRemember: אביי learns from עגלה ערופה, so designation counts. רבא learns from עבודה זרה, so designation alone does not count. Each one has a reason to reject the other's source.

phrases.english: He would say to you:
we learn something that is a proper practice from something that is a proper practice,
phrases.notes: Literally 'a thing that is its way'. He means a proper, permitted practice, like burial and the עגלה ערופה.

phrases.english: which excludes idol worship,
which is not a proper practice.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: מִידֵּי דְּאוֹרְחֵיהּ מִמִּידֵּי דְּאוֹרְחֵיהּ גָּמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about אביי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A proper מצוה practice should be learned from another proper practice, so idol worship is excluded.

steps.title: A memory aid for the coming challenges
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a סימן, a list of key words, to help remember the series of cases that will test the מחלוקת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Memory aid: scarf, monument, that was hewn, in his grave of one more than his father, in the craftsman's pouch.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is not an argument. It sets up the next part of the sugya by listing key words for the upcoming challenges, so the learner can keep track of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word is a hook for one case that will be brought against רבא or אביי. The first word, כפה (scarf), is the case that comes right after this step.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid, a list of key words
A scarf or head covering
A monument built over a grave
That was hewn (carved out)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not making a claim. It only lists key words for the cases that are coming next.

phrases.english: Memory aid: scarf, monument, that was hewn,
in his grave, of one more than his father,
phrases.notes: This is just a hook word for a grave case that comes later. Don't try to fully understand it yet.

phrases.english: in the craftsman's pouch.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the sources to testing the מחלוקת with cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. This is a list of key words for the coming cases.

steps.title: Challenge to רבא: a scarf designated for a ספר תורה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a scarf that was טמא מדרס loses that טומאה once it is set aside for a ספר תורה. That seems to show designation alone counts, which goes against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: a scarf that was טמא מדרס, and she set it aside for a ספר תורה, is pure from מדרס but impure with מגע מדרס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רבא. Setting the scarf aside for a holy book is enough to change its status, so designation seems to count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only an item meant for sitting or lying on can carry מדרס. Once the scarf is assigned to cover a ספר תורה, it is no longer that kind of item, so the מדרס leaves it. It still keeps a lighter טומאה from having touched the מדרס. If designation alone changes the scarf's status, then designation should count for shrouds too, against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure from a זב sitting or lying on it, a severe טומאה
And she gave it, here meaning she set it aside
A lighter טומאה from having touched something that was מדרס

phrases.english: They challenged:
A scarf that is impure with מדרס
and she set it aside for a ספר תורה,
is pure from מדרס,
but impure with the טומאה of touching מדרס.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the first case named in the סימן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that designation alone does not count
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Simply setting the scarf aside for a ספר תורה changes its טומאה status, which shows that designation does count.

steps.title: Reread it: she set it aside and wrapped it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא means she also wrapped the scarf around the scroll. A real action was done, not just designation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: she set it aside and wrapped it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by reading the ברייתא as including an action: the scarf was actually wrapped around the ספר תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא now has an action, wrapping, along with the designation. So the change in status can come from the action. The ברייתא no longer proves that designation alone counts, and רבא's view survives.

keyTerms.meaning: Say, read it as
And she wrapped it

steps.whatToRemember: The scarf case does not disprove רבא. Read the ברייתא as including actual wrapping, which is a real action and not mere designation.

phrases.english: Say:
she set it aside and wrapped it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא to include an action
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The scarf changed status through designation alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The scarf was also wrapped around the scroll. That action caused the change, so רבא's view still stands.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא mention both designating and wrapping?
steps.stepSummary: If wrapping the scarf around the ספר תורה was a real action, why does the ברייתא also say she designated it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need the ברייתא to say both that she set it aside and that she wrapped it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up on the last answer. If the action of wrapping is what matters, why does the ברייתא also mention designating the scarf?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6 the גמרא said the ברייתא means she also wrapped the scarf, so a real action was done. That seems to make the word 'designated' unnecessary. The גמרא wants to know why both are listed.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (a question about extra wording)
She gave it, meaning she designated it
She wrapped it

phrases.english: Why do I need 'she gave it and wrapped it'?
phrases.notes: 'Gave it' here means she set it aside for the ספר תורה. 'Wrapped it' is the action added in step 6.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording that results from the answer in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ברייתא needs both designation and wrapping if the action alone is what counts.

steps.title: Both are needed, as רב חסדא taught about a תפילין cloth
steps.stepSummary: Following רב חסדא, a cloth becomes restricted only when it is both designated for תפילין and actually used for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא follows רב חסדא. He said: a cloth that someone designated for wrapping תפילין, and then actually wrapped תפילין in it, may no longer be used for wrapping coins. If he only designated it and never used it, or used it without designating it first, he may still wrap coins in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both steps are needed. It quotes רב חסדא, who says a cloth becomes holy only when designation and use come together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using the cloth without designating it first is not enough. Designating it without using it is not enough either, which fits רבא. So the ברייתא lists both designating and wrapping, because together they change the scarf's status.

keyTerms.meaning: A cloth or scarf
תפילין, the boxes with פרשיות worn on the head and arm
He designated it
He bundled (wrapped) something in it
Small coins

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that using the cloth for תפילין alone makes it holy. רב חסדא says that use without earlier designation still leaves it permitted for coins.

phrases.english: It follows Rav Chisda,
for Rav Chisda said:
This cloth that one designated
to bundle tefillin in it,
and he did bundle tefillin in it –
it is forbidden to bundle coins in it.
If he designated it but did not bundle in it,
or he bundled in it but did not designate it –
it is permitted to bundle coins in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Designation and use are both needed for a holy status, as רב חסדא rules about a תפילין cloth.

steps.title: How אביי would state רב חסדא's rule
steps.stepSummary: According to אביי, designation alone already forbids the cloth for coins. Use without designation does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to אביי, who says designation counts: if he designated the cloth, it is forbidden for coins even if he never wrapped תפילין in it. If he wrapped תפילין in it, then if he had designated it, yes, it is forbidden. If he had not designated it, no, it is not forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how אביי would phrase רב חסדא's rule. For אביי, designation is the main thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's rule, as stated, fits רבא. For אביי, designation alone is enough to forbid the cloth. Use alone, without designation, still does nothing. So in both views use without designation does not count. The views differ only on designation without use.

keyTerms.meaning: Designation is a significant matter (it counts)
Yes
If

phrases.english: And according to Abaye, who said:
designation is a significant matter,

phrases.aramaic: אַזְמְנֵיהּ – אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא צַר בֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: if he designated it – even though he did not bundle in it, it is forbidden.
If he bundled in it: if he designated it – yes, it is forbidden,
if he did not designate it – no, it is not forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates רב חסדא's rule as אביי would hold it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For אביי, designation alone forbids the cloth for coins. Use without designation does not.

steps.title: A challenge from a monument built for a living person
steps.stepSummary: A monument built for a living person is permitted for use, but adding one row for the dead makes it forbidden. This seems to show designation alone counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a monument built for a living person may be used for benefit. If he added one row of stones to it for a dead person, it is forbidden for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to challenge רבא. It seems that just building a row for the dead, a kind of designation, makes the monument forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No body is mentioned in the case. So the row added for the dead seems to forbid the whole monument by designation alone. That supports אביי and goes against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: A monument built over or near a grave
A row or layer of stones
Forbidden to get any benefit from

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A monument that one built for a living person –
is permitted for benefit.

phrases.aramaic: הוֹסִיף בּוֹ דִּימוֹס אֶחָד לְשֵׁם מֵת –
phrases.english: If he added one row of stones to it for a dead person –
it is forbidden for benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: נֶפֶשׁ שֶׁבְּנָאוֹ לְשֵׁם חַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the scarf case is settled, a new case is brought against רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that designation alone does not count.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Adding a row for the dead, without mention of a body, forbids the monument. So designation seems to work by itself.

steps.title: A body was actually placed there
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a case where a dead body was put in the monument, which is a real action.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A case where a dead body was placed in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by explaining the case differently. A body was actually placed there, so it is forbidden because of an action, not only designation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the scarf answer in step 6, the גמרא adds a real action to the case. Once the body is placed, the prohibition comes from actual use for the dead. Then the ברייתא no longer proves anything about designation alone.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (used to narrow a source)
Placed, put down

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with here?
Where a dead body was placed in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The monument became forbidden through designation alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: A body was placed there, so a real action caused the prohibition.

steps.title: Then why mention the added row at all?
steps.stepSummary: If a body was placed there, the monument should be forbidden even without adding a row.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it say specifically that he added a row? Even if he did not add one, it should be forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own answer. If the body makes it forbidden, the detail about adding a row seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a body is placed in the monument, the whole monument has been used for the dead. So the added row adds nothing. The answer of step 11 seems to make the ברייתא's wording extra.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Why specifically this detail?
Also, too

phrases.english: If so, why specifically 'he added'?
Even if he did not add, it should be forbidden too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 11 based on the ברייתא's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that a body was placed in the monument.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the body is what forbids it, the detail of adding a row is not needed.

steps.title: It stays forbidden even after the body is removed
steps.stepSummary: The added row teaches that the monument stays forbidden even if the body is later taken out.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for the case where he later removed the body. Even then, it stays forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the added row matters. It teaches that the monument stays forbidden even after the body is moved away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the added row, removing the body might make the monument permitted again. Because a row was built for the dead and a body was placed there, the forbidden status stays even after the body is gone. So the detail is needed, and רבא's view still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this case
He removed it (cleared it out)

steps.whatToRemember: In both tests (the scarf and the monument), the גמרא protects רבא by showing a real action was done. Designation alone is never shown to be enough.

phrases.english: It is needed only
for a case where he removed it.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the dead body. Even after the body is taken out, the monument stays forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, אַף עַל גַּב דְּפַנְּיֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining why the extra detail is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The added row is pointless if a body was placed there.
steps.terutzMaskana: The added row teaches that the monument stays forbidden even after the body is removed.

steps.title: The added row can be removed, and the rest is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that if the added row of stones can be recognized, one may remove it, and the rest of the monument becomes permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם בר פפא said in the name of רב חסדא: if he can recognize the added row, he takes it out, and the monument is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a practical ruling about the monument case from the previous steps: only the extra row is forbidden, so removing it frees the rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said the added row keeps the monument forbidden even after the body is taken out. רב חסדא limits that: the forbidden part is only the row added for the dead. If that row can be identified and removed, the original structure, built for a living person, is permitted again.

keyTerms.meaning: He recognizes it (can tell which row was added)
He removes it / pulls it out
Permitted

phrases.english: Rafram bar Pappa said
that Rav Ḥisda said:
If he can recognize it,
phrases.notes: "It" is the extra row of stones added for the dead person, from the monument case in the earlier steps.

phrases.english: he removes it, and the rest is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical limit to the answer in step 13: only the added row stays forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the row added for the dead can be identified, it is removed and the rest of the monument is permitted.

steps.title: A grave dug for a father but not used
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that a son who dug a grave for his father, then buried him elsewhere, may never be buried in that grave. This suggests designation alone forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if someone dug a grave for his father, then went and buried him in a different grave, he himself may never be buried in the first one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא to challenge the view that designation alone does not forbid something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here no body was ever placed in the grave. It was only dug and meant for the father, yet it is forbidden forever. That looks like proof that designation by itself makes something forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: One who hews (digs/carves) a grave
Forever / never

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who hewed a grave for his father,
and then went and buried him in a different grave –

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יִקָּבֵר בּוֹ עוֹלָמִית.
phrases.english: this son may never be buried in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the monument challenge was answered, the גמרא brings a new source that seems to show designation alone counts.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that designation alone does not make something forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The grave was only prepared and never used, yet it is forbidden forever. So designation must be enough.

steps.title: The reason is the father's honor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the grave is forbidden to the son because of כבוד אביו, not because of designation.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is because of the honor of his father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by giving a different reason for the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son may not use the grave because it would be disrespectful to take for himself what he prepared for his father. That is a special rule about honoring a father. It says nothing about designation in general, so the challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in that case)
The honor owed to his father

steps.confusionAlert: The grave is not forbidden to everyone. The ruling only stops the son himself from using it, out of respect for his father.

phrases.english: There, it is because of the honor of his father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The grave is forbidden because it was designated for the dead.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is forbidden to the son only out of respect for his father, not because of designation.

steps.title: Support from the second half of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its answer with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling in the same ברייתא: even stones cut for the father's grave are forbidden to the son.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too it makes sense, since the end of the ברייתא teaches: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says, even if he cut stones for his father and then buried him somewhere else, he may never be buried with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a proof for its answer by quoting the end of the same ברייתא. The next step explains why this proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל goes further. Even stones that were only cut for the father's grave, not yet built into anything, may never be used for the son's own burial. That very early stage of preparation is the key to the proof in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it makes sense (introduces support for the answer just given)
The latter part of a teaching
Stones

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
since the latter clause teaches:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
even one who hewed stones for his father
and then went and buried him in a different place –

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יִקָּבֵר בָּהֶן עוֹלָמִית.
phrases.english: this son may never be buried with them.
phrases.notes: "Them" means the stones, so the son may never have his own tomb built from those stones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the answer in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That the grave is forbidden because of כבוד אביו, not designation
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end of the same ברייתא: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל on stones cut for the father

steps.title: Cut stones cannot count as designation
steps.stepSummary: The ruling about cut stones only makes sense if the reason is the father's honor, because no one treats such early preparation, like spinning thread for shrouds, as designation.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the reason is the father's honor, that works well. But if you say the reason is designation, is there anyone who says that spinning thread to weave it into shrouds counts as designation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof: the stones ruling fits only the reason of כבוד אביו, not הזמנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting stones is only an early step toward a grave, just like spinning thread that will later be woven into a shroud. Everyone agrees that spinning thread does not make it designated for the dead. So the stones cannot be forbidden because of designation, and the reason must be the father's honor. This confirms the answer in step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, if you say (this reason works well)
Well, fine
Designation (setting something aside for a purpose)
Spinning thread in order to weave it

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about a son who prepared a grave for his father cannot prove that designation forbids things. The rule exists because of כבוד אביו, as shown by the cut stones, which are far too early a stage to count as designation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This removes another source that seemed to prove designation alone forbids an item. The steps that follow keep testing the question of הזמנה with new sources.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא מִשּׁוּם כְּבוֹד אָבִיו –
phrases.english: Granted, if you say it is because of his father's honor –
it works well,
but if you say it is because of designation:
spinning thread in order to weave it
phrases.notes: He means spinning thread that will later be woven into burial shrouds. Cutting stones is as early a step as spinning that thread.

phrases.english: is there anyone who says it is designation?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא מִשּׁוּם כְּבוֹד אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the quote in step 17 supports the answer in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That the reason for the ruling is כבוד אביו
steps.raayaSupportSource: The cut-stones case, compared to spinning thread, which no one treats as designation
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The son's grave ruling comes from the father's honor, so it does not prove that designation forbids things.

steps.title: Proof from a new grave
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a new grave is permitted until a נפל is placed in it. This suggests that designation alone does not forbid it, which supports רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a new grave may be used for benefit. If a stillborn baby was placed in it, it becomes forbidden. So only if a body was placed in it is it forbidden; if not, it is not forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove רבא's view that designating something for the dead does not, by itself, make it forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A grave dug for burial has clearly been set aside for the dead. Yet the ברייתא says it becomes אסור בהנאה only once a body is actually placed inside. The גמרא reads this as proof that designation alone means nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: A new grave that has not yet been used
Forbidden to get any benefit from
A baby born not able to live (stillborn or dying soon after birth)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A new grave is permitted for benefit.
If he cast a stillborn baby into it, it is forbidden for benefit.
If he cast one in, yes; if he did not cast one in, no.
phrases.notes: This is the גמרא's own inference: the grave becomes forbidden only once a body is actually inside it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: קֶבֶר חָדָשׁ מוּתָּר בַּהֲנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending against the son's-grave challenge, the גמרא now looks for positive proof that designation does not forbid.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that designation alone (הזמנה) does not create a prohibition
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a new grave is forbidden only once a נפל is placed in it

steps.title: The stillborn is mentioned only to reject רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. A grave may be forbidden even without a body; the ברייתא mentions a נפל only to teach that even a נפל makes a grave forbidden, against רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same is true even if no body was placed in it. The ברייתא mentions a stillborn only to reject רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who says stillborn babies do not take hold of a grave. It teaches us that they do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from the new grave by giving another reason why the ברייתא mentions a נפל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference "only if a body was placed in it" is cancelled. The ברייתא's point is not that a body is needed. Its point is that even a נפל counts as a real body that makes a grave forbidden, which rejects רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view.

keyTerms.meaning: The same law applies
To exclude (to reject another opinion)
Taking hold of the grave, so that it becomes forbidden and belongs to the dead
It teaches us

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying a grave needs a body to become forbidden. It says the opposite is possible: even an empty grave may be forbidden. The נפל detail is there for a different reason.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא הַדִּין דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא הֵטִיל,
phrases.english: The same is true even though he did not cast one in,
and it mentions this to exclude the view of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל,
who says: stillborn babies do not take hold of the grave.
It teaches us otherwise.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is teaching that even a stillborn baby makes the grave forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא הַדִּין דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא הֵטִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference drawn from the words 'הטיל בו נפל', not the ברייתא itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The detail of the נפל was assumed to be a condition, but it actually comes to reject רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's opinion about נפלים

steps.title: Proof from leftover burial money
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says leftover money collected for a specific dead person goes to his heirs. Money set aside for him is not forbidden, which supports רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: leftover money collected for the dead goes to other dead. Leftover money collected for a particular dead person goes to his heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second proof for רבא from a משנה about money collected for burial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money collected to bury a specific person was clearly set aside for that dead person. If his heirs may keep and use whatever is left over, then designation alone did not make the money forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftover (extra money remaining)
His heirs

phrases.english: Come and hear: the leftover of money for the dead goes to the dead,
the leftover of money for a particular dead person goes to his heirs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that designation alone does not forbid
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in שקלים: leftover money for a particular dead person goes to his heirs

steps.title: The money was collected while he was alive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the משנה is talking about money collected while the person was still alive, so it was never set aside for a dead person.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where they collected the money while he was still alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the second proof by narrowing the case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the money was collected before the man died, it was never designated for a dead person at all. So the heirs inheriting it proves nothing about designation for the dead.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (used to narrow a source to a specific case)
During his lifetime

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with here?
Where they collected the money during his lifetime.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the משנה to a case of money collected before death
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the money was designated for a dead person, but it may have been collected while he was alive

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the money was collected after death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. A ברייתא explaining the משנה shows that the case is money collected for this specific dead person, after he died.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is not taught that way. We learned: leftover money for the dead goes to the dead, and leftover money for a particular dead person goes to his heirs. A ברייתא explains: How so? If they collected for the dead without specifying anyone, that is 'leftover for the dead goes to the dead.' If they collected for this dead person, that is 'leftover for the dead person goes to his heirs.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 22 by quoting a ברייתא that explains the משנה differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא describes the case as collecting "for this dead person", meaning he had already died. So the 'collected while alive' answer does not fit. The proof for רבא seems to come back.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is not taught that way
And a ברייתא taught about it (explaining the משנה)
How so?
Without specifying (in general)

phrases.english: But it is not taught that way,
as we learned: the leftover of money for the dead goes to the dead,
the leftover of money for a particular dead person goes to his heirs.
And it was taught about it: How so?
If they collected for the dead without specifying anyone,
this is 'the leftover for the dead goes to the dead.'
If they collected for this dead person,
this is 'the leftover for the dead person goes to his heirs.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the money was collected during the person's lifetime
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explaining the משנה describes money collected 'for this dead person', which means after death. So the 'collected while alive' answer cannot be right.

steps.title: The second half of the משנה seems to support אביי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers back: if the first opinion supports רבא, the opinions of רבי מאיר and רבי נתן in the same משנה seem to support אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your reasoning, look at the end of the משנה: רבי מאיר says the leftover money may not be touched until אליהו comes. רבי נתן says it should be used for a row of stones on his grave or for sprinkling fragrant wine before his bier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the attack from step 23 by pointing to the end of the same משנה. There, two תנאים treat the leftover money as if it does become forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר will not let anyone use the money, and רבי נתן says it must be spent on the dead person. That sounds like designation (הזמנה) does make the money forbidden, which is אביי's view. So this משנה can't be a clean proof for רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning: turning the other side's argument back on them
The latter part of a משנה or ברייתא
Until אליהו comes: leave the matter unresolved until he clarifies it
A row of stones built over a grave
Sprinkling fragrant wine or perfume

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
say the latter clause:
phrases.notes: The end of the same משנה about leftover money collected for a dead person, from step 21.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says,
one may not touch it
until Elijah comes.
Rabbi Natan says:
he should use it for a row of stones over his grave
or for sprinkling before his bier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 23 by showing the משנה is two-sided, so it cannot settle the dispute.
steps.kashyaTarget: The attempt to prove רבא's view from the first opinion in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The end of the same משנה has opinions that treat designated money as forbidden, which fits אביי. So the משנה as a whole proves nothing for רבא.

steps.title: Each אמורא can explain the whole משנה his own way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that both אביי and רבא can explain the entire משנה according to their own views.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי explains the משנה according to his reasoning, and רבא explains it according to his reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא announces that this משנה can fit both views, and the next steps will show how each one explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of using the משנה as a proof for one side, the גמרא says it is neutral. Each אמורא will explain all three opinions in a way that fits his own position.

keyTerms.meaning: Explains the source according to his own reasoning

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye explains it according to his reasoning,
and Rava explains it according to his reasoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אַבָּיֵי מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ וְרָבָא מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from step 24: the משנה cannot decide the dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The source is neutral and each side can read it his own way
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to prove רבא's view, or perhaps אביי's.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה fits both views, so it proves nothing.

steps.title: אביי's reading: the first תנא forbids only what was fitting to spend
steps.stepSummary: According to אביי, all three תנאים agree that designation makes money forbidden. The first תנא holds that only the amount fitting for this burial becomes forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי explains it his way: everyone agrees that designation counts. The first תנא holds that the amount that is fitting for the dead person becomes forbidden, and the amount that is not fitting does not become forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains why the first תנא gives leftover money to the heirs, even though אביי holds that designation forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, the first תנא is not saying designation has no effect. The designation only takes hold of the amount actually suitable for this burial. The extra money was never forbidden, so it goes to the heirs.

keyTerms.meaning: Designation is significant: setting something aside for the dead already makes it forbidden
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא
Literally "takes hold": here, becomes included in the prohibition

phrases.english: Abaye explains it according to his reasoning:
according to everyone, designation is a significant matter.
The first tanna holds:
what is fitting for him is included in the prohibition,
phrases.notes: He means the amount that is right to spend on this person's burial.

phrases.english: what is not fitting for him is not included.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא הַזְמָנָה מִילְּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins carrying out the plan from step 25, starting with אביי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the prohibition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Giving leftover money to the heirs seemed to show designation has no effect.
steps.terutzMaskana: Designation does forbid, but only the amount fitting for the burial. The extra was never forbidden.

steps.title: אביי's reading of רבי מאיר and רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: According to אביי, רבי מאיר is unsure whether the extra money becomes forbidden, so he leaves it alone. רבי נתן is sure it does become forbidden, so it must be spent on the dead person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר is unsure whether it becomes forbidden or not, so one may not touch it until אליהו comes. And it is obvious to רבי נתן that it certainly becomes forbidden, so it should be used for a row of stones over his grave.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his explanation by fitting the other two opinions into his view that designation counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three agree that designation forbids. They only argue about the extra money beyond what is fitting. The first תנא says it is not included, רבי מאיר is in doubt, and רבי נתן says it is definitely included.

keyTerms.meaning: He is uncertain about it
It is obvious to him
Therefore

steps.whatToRemember: For אביי, all three תנאים agree designation forbids. They only argue about the extra money: the first תנא says it is not forbidden, רבי מאיר is unsure, and רבי נתן says it is surely forbidden.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir is uncertain about it,
phrases.notes: His doubt is only about the extra money that wasn't fitting to spend.

phrases.english: whether it is included or not included.
Therefore, one may not touch it
until Elijah comes.
And to Rabbi Natan it is obvious
that it is certainly included,
therefore it should be used for a row of stones over his grave.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ, אִי תָּפֵיס אִי לָא תָּפֵיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's explanation, which began in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasting the dispute as a question about how far the prohibition reaches
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The three opinions seemed to argue about whether designation counts at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: They agree designation counts and only argue about whether the extra money is included.

steps.title: רבא's reading: the dead person gives up his honor for his heirs
steps.stepSummary: According to רבא, all three תנאים agree that designation does not forbid. The first תנא holds that the dead person gives up the disgrace of the collection so that his heirs can benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא explains it his way: according to everyone, designation is not significant. The first תנא holds that even though they disgraced him, he gives up his disgrace for the sake of his heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: Now רבא starts his own explanation of the same משנה. He says nobody in the משנה holds that designation forbids, so the argument must be about something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the dispute is not about a prohibition at all. It is about the dead person's honor: collecting money for his burial was a disgrace to him. The first תנא says he forgives that disgrace for his heirs, so they get the extra money.

keyTerms.meaning: Designation is nothing: setting something aside does not make it forbidden
They disgraced him
He fully forgives or gives up
Heirs

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבא is reading the משנה as being about a prohibition. In his reading, the whole argument is about the dead person's honor, since for him designation forbids nothing.

phrases.english: And Rava explains it according to his reasoning:

phrases.aramaic: לְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא הַזְמָנָה לָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא.
phrases.english: according to everyone, designation is not a significant matter.
The first tanna holds:
when they disgraced him,
phrases.notes: Collecting money for his burial in public was a disgrace to the dead person.

phrases.english: he forgives his disgrace for the sake of the heirs.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ: לְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא הַזְמָנָה לָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבא's explanation, a parallel to אביי's in steps 26 and 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the dispute to a different issue (the dead person's honor)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The opinions of רבי מאיר and רבי נתן seemed to show that designation forbids.
steps.terutzMaskana: Nobody holds designation forbids. The argument is only about whether the dead person forgives his disgrace for his heirs.

steps.title: רבא's reading of רבי מאיר and רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: According to רבא, רבי מאיר is unsure whether the dead person gives up his disgrace, so the leftover money is left alone. רבי נתן is sure he does not give it up, so the leftover is spent on honoring him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר is unsure whether the dead person forgives the disgrace or does not, so the money may not be touched. And רבי נתן is sure he does not forgive it, so the extra money is used for a row of stones over his grave or for sprinkling fragrant wine before his bier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues רבא's explanation of the משנה and now explains the views of רבי מאיר and רבי נתן. For רבא, their dispute is only about whether the dead person gives up his disgrace.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 27, אביי explained the same two opinions as a doubt about whether designation forbids. Here רבא keeps the same rulings but changes the reason: designation does not forbid, and the only question is מחילה. If the dead person may not forgive the disgrace (רבי מאיר), we cannot let the heirs use the money. If he surely does not forgive it (רבי נתן), the money must be used for his honor.

keyTerms.meaning: He is unsure, it is a doubt for him
Forgives, gives up (here: the disgrace of the collection)
It is obvious to him
A row of stones built over a grave
Sprinkling fragrant wine or spices

steps.whatToRemember: Both אביי and רבא accept the same rulings in the משנה. אביי says the dispute is about whether designation forbids. רבא says designation never forbids, and the dispute is only about whether the dead person gives up his disgrace.
steps.confusionAlert: The rulings here are exactly the same as in אביי's version (step 27). Only the reason behind them is different, so don't look for a different practical outcome.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir is uncertain
whether he forgoes or does not forgo,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the dead person, and what he might give up is the disgrace of having money collected for him.

phrases.english: therefore, one may not touch them, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' points to the rest of the line in the משנה: the money waits until אליהו comes.

phrases.english: And to Rabbi Natan it is obvious
that he does not forgo,
therefore, a row of stones should be made over his grave
or sprinkling before his bier.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ אִי מַחֵיל אִי לָא מַחֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's reading of the משנה that step 28 began with the first תנא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 24 that רבי מאיר and רבי נתן support אביי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the same rulings are explained by a different reason (מחילה rather than designation).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rulings of רבי מאיר and רבי נתן seemed to show that designation forbids, which would support אביי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their rulings fit רבא too, since they may depend only on whether the dead person forgives his disgrace.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה cannot decide between אביי and רבא, because each can explain all three opinions.

steps.title: A new proof attempt: parents throwing garments onto the bier
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: if a dead man's father and mother throw garments onto him, others should save the garments. This is set up as a possible proof for רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if his father and mother were throwing garments onto him, it is a מצוה for the others to save them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new proof attempt with 'תא שמע' and quotes a ברייתא about parents throwing clothes onto their son's bier. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will see whether this case proves רבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The parents clearly meant the garments for the dead person, yet the ברייתא tells others to rescue them. If designation alone made things forbidden, the garments would already be forbidden and there would be no point in saving them. So this case seems to support רבא, who says designation does not forbid.

keyTerms.meaning: Throwing, tossing
Here: garments or clothing
To save them, to rescue them from being lost

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the next test of the אביי/רבא argument after the משנה turned out to fit both views.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If his father and his mother were
throwing garments onto him,
it is a מצוה for the others to save them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הָיוּ אָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ מְזָרְקִין בּוֹ כֵּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה turned out to fit both אביי and רבא, the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that designation alone does not make an item forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: when parents throw garments onto their son's bier, others should save the garments. This suggests the garments did not become forbidden just by being meant for the dead.
